ety.text: Perhaps from Proto-Italic *arks, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂érk-s, from the root *h₂erk- (“to protect, guard, hold, lock”). De Vaan suggests that the root noun may have been formed innovatively within Proto-Italic itself or perhaps at an even later date. Cognates include Latin arca (“chest, box”), arceō (“to defend”), arcānus (“hidden, secret”), arcera (“covered carriage for sick people”), Old Armenian արգել (argel, “obstacle”) and Ancient Greek ἀρκέω (arkéō, “to ward off, fend off”), Persian ارگ (arg, “citadel”)
